author: noel_reports
text: ❗️ Russian attacks hit energy infrastructure in Ukraine’s Vinnytsia and Zhytomyr regions. More than 650 settlements in Zhytomyr region were left without power. Vinnytsia also reported damage to a mobile tower, warehouse, apartment windows, public transport infrastructure and a vehicle.

author: noel_reports
text: ❗️ Ukraine’s Unmanned Systems Forces say October was their strongest month of the full-scale war by several metrics. Commander Robert “Magyar” Brovdi reports 64,807 Russian targets struck during 255,605 combat missions, including 151,500 strike and 104,000 reconnaissance sorties. He says 16,796 Russian personnel were verified killed or wounded, 24.7% more than in September. Around 69.5% of those losses were recorded on the Dobropillia-Pokrovsk, Oleksandrivka and Huliaipole axes.

author: noel_reports
text: Swedish police boarded the cargo ship Germanica Hav off Gotland after reports that it had been moving suspiciously near a military training area. TV4 says the National Task Force took part. The vessel’s operator, which has links to Norway and Kaliningrad and reportedly uses largely Russian crews, has previously been scrutinized over suspected Russian hybrid and reconnaissance activity. Police publicly described the operation as a routine border check.

author: noel_reports
text: Zelensky says Russia struck Ukraine’s energy infrastructure in four regions overnight, leaving hundreds of thousands of families without power. Over the past week, Russia launched 1,940 strike drones, more than 1,580 guided bombs and 44 missiles, including 36 ballistic missiles.

author: noel_reports
text: Footage captured by another drone shows a Ukrainian interceptor drone taking down a Russian Shahed. Operators from the 413th Separate Unmanned Systems Regiment “Raid” detected and destroyed the target.

author: noel_reports
text: Zelensky says Ukrainian long-range strikes hit the Kamensky Combine in Russia’s Rostov region, a defense plant involved in missile production. A Pantsir-S2 system and an S-400 command vehicle were also struck. He put the combined value of the damaged air-defense assets at about $70 million.

author: noel_reports
text: The Times reports that Putin increasingly frames Russia’s war against Ukraine through medieval history, drawing parallels between today’s confrontation with the West and the struggles of figures such as Alexander Nevsky. The newspaper says his fixation on correcting what he sees as historical injustices is causing concern even in Moscow. A source close to the Kremlin told The Times: “He never lost touch with reality. Now, I don’t know.”

author: noel_reports
text: Ukraine’s 412th Nemesis Brigade says its RETRO crew used a new auto-guided ZIRKA interceptor drone to shoot down a Russian Geran-5 jet-powered drone at 3,500 meters. The target was flying at roughly 400 km/h.

author: noel_reports
text: OSINT Бджоли reports that the October 21 Su-30SM crash in Russia’s Kaliningrad region involved more than one aircraft. Imagery reportedly shows a second Su-30SM damaged in the same incident. Based on the visible damage, an in-air collision is a possible explanation.

author: noel_reports
text: Russia keeps adding improvised protection around critical infrastructure. Alongside multilayer anti-drone nets, shipping containers have now been positioned around key equipment needed to keep an energy facility operating, another sign of the growing pressure from Ukrainian long-range strikes.

author: noel_reports
text: Ukrainian forces continue systematically striking Russian logistics in Donetsk region. Footage from September-October shows two fuel tankers destroyed near Pokrovsk and Manhush, an ammunition truck near Novokrasnovka that detonated after the strike, and another cargo truck near Zlatoustivka.

author: noel_reports
text: ❗️ Another large-scale Russian missile and drone attack may take place within the next 24 hours. Six Tu-95MS and Tu-160 bombers are prepared, with additional aircraft possible, alongside at least 30 Iskander, S-400, Zircon and Oniks missiles. Energy infrastructure, including substations, heating, gas and power facilities, as well as logistics and railway infrastructure, are listed as likely targets.

author: noel_reports
text: Kramatorsk, another Ukrainian frontline city being steadily scarred by Russia’s war. October footage from the 24th Mechanized Brigade shows the growing destruction. Bakhmut, Soledar, Avdiivka and Mar’inka are reminders of what happens when a city remains in Russia’s path for too long.

author: noel_reports
text: A convoy of ambulances was spotted in Kyiv carrying residents evacuated from Russian-occupied Oleshky to hospitals in the capital. The evacuees have now reached Ukrainian-controlled territory following the humanitarian operation.

author: noel_reports
text: A major fire is burning at the Kotovo Pole shopping center in Russia’s Leningrad region. The cause of the blaze is currently unknown.

author: noel_reports
text: ❗️ You can’t make this up. Sportbladet reports Ukraine could be dropped from the 2027 ice hockey IIHF World Championship elite division to make room for Russia, after CAS cleared a Russian return. Ukraine had just earned promotion for the first time in 20 years. No final decision has been made.

author: noel_reports
text: This is how Ukrainians welcomed people returning today from Russian occupation. Oleshky is only one of many occupied cities, and thousands of Ukrainians are still waiting to come home. They have not been forgotten. Ukraine remembers its people under occupation.

author: noel_reports
text: Unexpected, but credit where credit is due. NEWSMAX correspondent Shelby Wilder says Russia is using the humanitarian operation in occupied Oleshky for propaganda while tightly controlling what journalists can see. She warned that access is restricted and residents allowed to speak with media may be under pressure.

author: noel_reports
text: Good night, sleep well and see you all tomorrow.

The facility is one of Russia’s largest refineries, processing roughly 15-17 million tonnes of crude annually. It produces large volumes of gasoline, diesel and aviation fuel, making it an important node in Russia’s fuel supply system.

author: noel_reports
text: Trump says he would invite Zelensky to the G20 summit in Miami on December 14-15. Asked whether Zelensky would be invited given that Putin has already been invited, Trump replied: “I would. I would. No problem.”

text: The Novomoskovsk Azot chemical plant in Russia’s Tula region is still burning this morning following the overnight strike.

text: A Ukrainian MiG-29MU1 fighter engaged a Russian drone using both an R-60 short-range air-to-air missile and its onboard cannon.

author: noel_reports
text: Zelensky says Putin does not feel sufficient pressure from Washington because Trump publicly emphasizes his good relationship with the Russian leader. “When Trump shows that he has a wonderful relationship with Putin, Putin sees it in the media and understands that everything is fine. There is no pressure,” Zelensky said. He added that the US too rarely condemns Russian aggression strongly enough.

author: noel_reports
text: Russian Il-76 transport aircraft carrying residents evacuated from occupied Oleshky have arrived in Belarus. The passengers are those who chose to return to Ukrainian-controlled territory as part of the ongoing humanitarian operation.

author: noel_reports
text: Zelensky and his delegation have arrived in Istanbul for talks with Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan. Zelensky says discussions will focus on strengthening Ukraine’s defense, bilateral cooperation, diplomatic prospects and Black Sea shipping. He will also meet Ecumenical Patriarch Bartholomew.

author: noel_reports
text: Zelensky says the humanitarian operation in Russian-occupied Oleshky has been completed successfully. During the ceasefire, roads into the city were demined, humanitarian aid was delivered and residents needing evacuation were taken out. Ukrainian citizens from Oleshky have now crossed back into Ukraine through Chernihiv region. Zelensky thanked US First Lady Melania Trump for mediation, Ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets and Ukraine’s Defense Forces for securing the mission.

author: noel_reports
text: Residents evacuated from Russian-occupied Oleshky have now reached Ukrainian-controlled territory. Ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets says the oldest evacuee is 94 and the youngest just over one year old. One family had been trapped in a heavily damaged apartment building because the father could not descend from the eighth floor after the stairs were destroyed. Another man survived 16 Russian drone attacks and four missile strikes on his home. Their pets were evacuated too.

author: noel_reports
text: Satellite imagery analysis indicates the October 30 Ukrainian drone strike on Russia’s Novokuybyshevsk refinery was one of the most damaging attacks on a Russian refinery this year. Significant damage was identified at the AVT-9 and AVT-11 crude distillation units, a diesel hydrotreating unit, two nearby unidentified installations and parts of the refinery’s tank farms. The actual impact on refining capacity still needs to be determined.

author: noel_reports
text: The US Embassy in Moscow has issued a security alert warning of a “credible threat of a mass casualty event” today, October 31, at the Tsaritsyno Museum Reserve in Moscow. US citizens are being urged to avoid the area, stay alert, avoid crowds and monitor local media. The embassy says the US government is coordinating with appropriate Russian authorities on a response. No further details about the nature of the threat were provided.

author: noel_reports
text: Fire Point co-founder and chief designer Denys Shtilerman says the FP-7 ballistic missile has already seen combat use, but its current high-explosive fragmentation version is too expensive for routine employment. He says delivering a 200 kg payload over 300 km costs about $600,000 with FP-7, compared with roughly $50,000 using an FP-2. Shtilerman says the missile makes more sense once a cluster-warhead version is codified. He added that FP-9 is in final testing.

author: noel_reports
text: European aerospace company Destinus says it has completed 1,750 Ruta B1 cruise missiles, with monthly production now close to 300 units. The company says the system has moved from prototype production to full serial manufacturing. Destinus also produces the T150 turbojet engine, navigation system, airframe, guidance and avionics in-house, giving it control over most of the missile’s core production chain.

author: noel_reports
text: Zelensky says Ukraine and Turkey agreed to work together on restoring the Black Sea grain corridor following his meeting with President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan. He also proposed holding trilateral negotiations in Turkey with the participation of Europe and other international partners. Kyiv says it wants Turkey and European states more directly involved in efforts aimed at ending Russia’s war against Ukraine.

author: noel_reports
text: Marco Rubio offered a far more cautious assessment of Ukraine peace talks than Trump: “I don’t know if negotiated peace is achievable. Nobody is claiming we are on the verge.” Rubio said Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff are working on the issue full-time. Trump had said hours earlier that an end to the war could be near.

author: noel_reports
text: Canadian manufacturer Roshel says nearly 3,000 Senator armored vehicles have now gone to Ukraine. That makes the Senator one of the most numerous Western-supplied armored vehicles in Ukrainian service. Ukraine uses them to transport troops, evacuate wounded personnel and conduct patrol and reconnaissance missions. Canada has funded part of the fleet, while other donor countries and Ukraine itself have also purchased vehicles.

author: noel_reports
text: Russia launched 168 drones at Ukraine between 06:30 and 19:30 on October 31, including 51 jet-powered drones, plus S8000 Banderol/Dan-T systems, the Air Force says. Ukrainian defenses shot down or suppressed 122 drones, including 37 jet-powered ones, and two S8000s. Around 30 drones remain airborne.

author: noel_reports
text: ❗️ Multiple Russian-type drones crossed Moldova and Romania on October 31, triggering RO-Alerts in Iași and Neamț and the scrambling of four Romanian F-16s and a helicopter. One Gerbera later crossed from Romania into Ukraine, where Ukrainian forces shot it down near Krasnoilsk.

author: noel_reports
text: Former presidents Aleksandar Vučić and Viktor Orbán struck a defiant tone together: “We will return.” Vučić added: “Yes, we both recently lost elections, but we have not lost our dignity, our pride or our faith.”

text: A major blackout hit Russia’s Kaliningrad exclave around midnight, affecting parts of Kaliningrad city and several surrounding towns. Russian officials say emergency protection systems at the 900 MW CHP-2 plant shut down part of the equipment, but have not explained what caused the system to trip. Load was shifted to other generating facilities and power is gradually being restored. There is scattered speculation about sabotage or an attack, but no evidence has been presented.

author: noel_reports
text: ❗️ Ukraine has clearly restarted its campaign against Russian oil refineries. After yesterday’s large-scale strike on Novokuybyshevsk, Ufa is now the latest target, with a fire reported at the refining complex in Bashkortostan. Located roughly 1,300-1,500 km from Ukraine, the Ufa hub is one of Russia’s largest refining centers and produces gasoline, diesel, lubricants and aviation fuel used across civilian and military logistics.

text: Ukrainian forces carried out a combined missile and drone strike on the Kamensky Combine in Kamensk-Shakhtinsky, Rostov region, on October 31. At least four workshops were damaged, while a warehouse storing finished products caught fire. The facility is described as a key Russian defense-industrial producer of solid rocket fuel and explosives used in multiple-launch rocket systems and air-defense complexes.

author: noel_reports
text: Major disruptions are being reported across Moscow as Ukrainian drone activity affects the region. Airports have suspended operations, while something is burning near Sheremetyevo Airport after an air-raid warning. Local reports suggest a drone may have been intercepted, but this remains unconfirmed.

author: noel_reports
text: Ukraine’s Defense Minister Yevhen Khmara and Commander-in-Chief Mykhailo Drapatyi held a joint meeting on the front-line situation, Russia’s plans including mobilization, possible enemy actions, key security risks and urgent needs of the Defense Forces. They also discussed countering air attacks, expanding Ukraine’s defense-industrial production and planning combat operations at both tactical and operational depth.

author: noel_reports
text: Zelensky says Ukrainian deep-strike drones and missiles can now reach Russian targets along a line stretching from Yamal to Western Siberia, and that work is underway to extend that reach even farther. He says Ukraine will scale up deep-strike units based on the capabilities of the SBU, including the Alpha Special Operations Center, as well as military intelligence and other parts of the Defense Forces. Zelensky called long-range strike capability a key guarantee of Ukraine’s security.

author: noel_reports
text: Ukraine’s Navy says two Russian Su-34 fighter-bombers were destroyed at Marinovka airfield in Volgograd region by a Neptune missile strike. The aircraft were based with the 11th Composite Aviation Regiment of Russia’s 4th Air Force and Air Defense Army.

author: noel_reports
text: ❗️ ❗️ Russian aviation taking another beating. Ukraine’s 3rd Assault Brigade says it destroyed a Russian Mi-8 helicopter using a Hornet drone equipped with automatic guidance.

author: noel_reports
text: Fire Point says its weapons are designed to complete missions without Starlink, using navigation that can function without external signals. CEO Iryna Terekh says the 300-km FP-7 ballistic missile could be used against mobile Russian Iskander launchers, potentially offering a cheaper offensive alternative to intercepting their missiles with Patriots. She also says the longer-range FP-9, designed for about 800 km, is “very close” to combat readiness and could be ready this year.

author: noel_reports
text: ❗️ Ukraine and Hungary are preparing an intergovernmental commission next month as Budapest continues blocking the final EU accession clusters, Foreign Ministry spokesperson Heorhii Tykhyi says. Talks will cover a broad agenda, including economic issues and minority rights.

author: noel_reports
text: ❗️ Exilenova+ published exclusive footage showing the first minutes after Storm Shadow cruise missiles struck production buildings at a Russian defense plant in Yelets, Lipetsk region. They also released a photo from inside one of the damaged facilities, showing a workshop extensively destroyed.

author: noel_reports
text: The US State Department has approved a possible $2.1 billion sale of 500 PAC-3 MSE missiles for Ukraine’s Patriot systems. Canada, Germany and Norway will finance the package, which also includes spare parts, logistics and technical support. No delivery timeline was announced. That is important, as the missiles are likely to come from new production rather than existing US stocks, which have been heavily drawn down during the war with Iran.

author: noel_reports
text: Trump called people who wanted him to impose sanctions on Russia during negotiations “stupid,” arguing sanctions would have undermined efforts to secure the release of American Stephen Hubbard. “They wanted me, while negotiating, to put sanctions on Russia,” Trump said.

author: noel_reports
text: Poland’s constitutional crisis escalated after Constitutional Tribunal chief Bogdan Święczkowski was suspended and police secured the court building in Warsaw. Opposition leader Jarosław Kaczyński accused Donald Tusk’s government of attempting a “coup,” while the government says it is restoring the rule of law after years of politicization under PiS. President Karol Nawrocki cut short a foreign trip and is returning to Warsaw.

author: noel_reports
text: Russian strikes caused water outages in Kyiv’s Obolon district, while parts of the capital also lost electricity. DTEK says partial power cuts affected Obolonskyi, Darnytskyi, Desnianskyi and Podilskyi districts. Repair crews are working to restore services.

author: noel_reports
text: A NASA satellite captured the moment of a Russian ballistic missile strike on Kyiv from space, showing the flash from the impact over the Ukrainian capital.

author: noel_reports
text: A Russian drone struck a bridge in Dnipro, according to local reports. The extent of the damage and whether there are casualties is not yet clear.

author: noel_reports
text: ❗️ The traditional G20 group photo was reportedly canceled after several foreign ministers refused to pose alongside Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov, Bloomberg reports. Germany’s Johann Wadephul said there can be “no business as usual” with Russia.

ABSreliable says this would be the fourth Su-57 lost in 2026, after two aircraft were hit at Shagol earlier in the year and another was reportedly downed by friendly fire in Moscow region on July 23.

author: noel_reports
text: Zelensky confirmed in his yesterday evening address that Ukrainian forces carried out two missile strikes, destroying two Russian Su-34 fighter-bombers and striking an Iskander launcher. He thanked the units involved for the result.

author: noel_reports
text: Destinus says it has built more than 1,750 Ruta cruise missiles in Europe and is now producing nearly 300 per month. For Ukraine, one of the most important developments is propulsion: CEO Mikhail Kokorich says Destinus expects from 2027 to be able to meet European and Ukrainian demand for 1.5-kN turbojet engines, an area that has constrained Ukraine’s ability to scale jet-powered weapons. The larger Ruta Block 2, with a 250-kg payload and range above 700 km, has also entered production.

author: noel_reports
text: Ukraine’s CERT-UA says the UAC-0050 hacking group launched a new phishing campaign against government institutions, posing as DTEK Energy staff. Emails about alleged electricity debt lead victims through malicious archives that install LiteManager for persistent remote access.

author: noel_reports
text: Presidential Office Head Kyrylo Budanov says the humanitarian operation in Russian-occupied Oleshky should continue. Humanitarian aid has already reached the city, while transport has been prepared for residents who want to evacuate to Ukrainian-controlled territory.

author: noel_reports
text: ❗️ The Trump administration is pressing Lithuania to reopen Klaipėda port for Belarusian potash exports despite EU sanctions, Politico reports. US envoy John Coale has reportedly sounded out Lithuanian diplomats in recent weeks about easing restrictions. Washington wants to reduce US dependence on Canadian potash and lower costs for American farmers. One Eastern European official described Lithuania’s response as: “No, damn it.”

author: noel_reports
text: 17 Buses full of Ukrainian locals will be evacuated from occupied Oleshky to Ukrainian territory.

author: noel_reports
text: Operators of Ukraine’s SIGNUM Battalion, part of the 59th Separate Assault Battalion of Unmanned Systems, struck a fully loaded Russian BM-21 Grad multiple rocket launcher just as it was preparing to fire. The system was destroyed before it could launch its salvo.

author: noel_reports
text: Ukrainian Ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets reassured residents in Russian-occupied Oleshky who fear pressure from Russian forces: “We will take everyone. No one will do anything to you.” The humanitarian evacuation operation is continuing.

author: noel_reports
text: Ukraine’s State Bureau of Investigation says it stopped the illegal sale of a BRDM-2 armored reconnaissance vehicle and explosives equivalent to about 300 kg of TNT. A former deputy commander of a mechanized brigade and an accomplice were detained while allegedly trying to sell the package for $8,000.

author: noel_reports
text: Ukrainian media have published exclusive footage from Russian-occupied Oleshky as residents are evacuated toward Ukrainian-controlled territory. One woman summed up the moment in a few words: “I’m going because I missed my children so much.” The footage also captures residents describing life under occupation and the emotions surrounding the long-awaited humanitarian mission. Evacuees are being taken out through Anapa.

author: noel_reports
text: Ukraine’s 125th Heavy Mechanized Brigade says it has been rebuilt over the past year after joining the 3rd Army Corps. In October 2025 it reported just 17% staffing, no tanks, artillery or armored vehicles, and almost no drone crews. It now says core units are 95-100% staffed, 1,500 personnel have returned from unauthorized absence, and reconnaissance, FPV, heavy bomber drone and ground robotic units have expanded sharply. The brigade now operates Bradley IFVs, Leopard tanks and artillery.

author: noel_reports

author: noel_reports
text: Ukraine says Russia launched Iskander-M, S-400 and KN-23 ballistic missiles, four Kh-59/69 guided missiles and 113 drones overnight, including 83 jet-powered Shaheds. Air defenses reportedly shot down or suppressed 99 targets: 3 Kh-59/69 missiles and 96 drones, including 71 jet-powered Shaheds. Kyiv, Poltava and Dnipropetrovsk regions were the main targets. Impacts were recorded at 17 locations and debris at five more.

author: noel_reports
text: ❗️ NATO allies are increasingly concerned that additional US-made Patriot interceptors for Ukraine may be delayed until after the November 3 midterms, Euronews reports. Zelensky says Kyiv is still waiting for US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth to approve the transfer. NATO sources called the situation “unpredictable” and said allies have little clarity on whether the missiles will be released or when they might arrive.

author: noel_reports
text: ❗️ Russia’s Novokuybyshevsk oil refinery in Samara region is heavily ablaze after an overnight Ukrainian drone attack, with at least 6 and reportedly 11 separate fires across the complex. The Rosneft-operated facility processes roughly 8.8 million tons of crude annually and produces aviation kerosene, gasoline and diesel. The refinery is an important supplier within Russia’s fuel and military logistics network.

author: noel_reports
text: Ukraine reportedly struck the Konservsushprod plant in Starodub, Bryansk region overnight. The factory produces combat rations, canned meat and other shelf-stable food for Russian personnel and supplies the Defense Ministry, Interior Ministry and Rosgvardia.

author: noel_reports
text: Ukraine’s Navy says two Russian Su-34 fighter-bombers were destroyed at Marinovka airfield in Volgograd region by a Neptune missile strike. The aircraft were based with the 11th Composite Aviation Regiment of Russia’s 4th Air Force and Air Defense Army.

author: noel_reports
text: Zelensky confirmed in his yesterday evening address that Ukrainian forces carried out two missile strikes, destroying two Russian Su-34 fighter-bombers and striking an Iskander launcher . He thanked the units involved for the result.

author: noel_reports
text: Satellite imagery analyzed by DniproOsint shows the aftermath of the strike on the Taman substation. According to the analysis, the September 24 attack disrupted electricity supplies to parts of Russian-occupied Crimea.

author: noel_reports
text: The ceasefire around Russian-occupied Oleshky has now lasted more than 75 hours without a recorded violation, Ukrainian Ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets says, calling it the longest truce since 2022. The humanitarian mission is coordinating from Armyansk and has prepared 25 buses with 750 evacuation places, plus ambulances for people with limited mobility. Civilians who wish to leave will be offered safe evacuation, while those remaining will receive aid.

author: noel_reports
text: Some more shots from the Novokuybyshevsk refinery in Samara region.

author: noel_reports
text: Former CNN anchor Rick Sanchez, who now works for Russian state-controlled RT, is pushing Moscow’s narrative around Oleshky. Talking about the humanitarian operation, he blamed Ukraine for “the flooding” and repeated claims about attacks on ambulances, saying: “You have to take all the parts of the story into account.” That context matters. Sanchez isn’t some former CNN journalist giving an outside, independent take. He now works for Russian state media, and he’s repeating the same talking points the Kremlin is using around Oleshky.

author: noel_reports
text: The US is doing Russia a favour. Reuters reports that Pentagon officials have privately urged several NATO allies, including Lithuania, Latvia and Estonia, to tone down public rhetoric about Russia. One European official summarized the message as: “We are helping you. Just don’t be loud. Don’t make noise.”

author: noel_reports
text: Ukraine plans to build 21 alternative river crossings, including routes across the Dnipro, according to the Restoration Ministry. Work has already begun in Kyiv. The first crossings are expected to become operational in early 2027, expanding alternative transport links across major waterways.

author: noel_reports
text: Ukraine’s delegation has safely arrived in Russian-occupied Oleshky, Ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets says. The ceasefire has now held for 80 hours and remains in effect. Lubinets says he is speaking directly with local residents to understand their needs and determine what assistance is most urgently required. The mission is continuing under arrangements coordinated with Russian human rights representative Yana Lantratova.

author: noel_reports
text: Ukrainian presidential adviser Serhii “Flash” says Russian Geran-5 drones have reached speeds of up to 1,000 km/h while maneuvering. He estimates Russia produces up to 3,000 jet-powered Shaheds and around 700 Geran-5 drones per month. Flash also says Russia is introducing AI into Molniya, Geran and Lancet drones so they can autonomously identify and attack targets including trains, warehouses and vehicles.

author: noel_reports
text: ❗️ The European Commission is proposing another €21.3 billion under the SAFE program for EU defense procurement and is urging member states to involve Ukraine in joint purchases. Priority areas include air and missile defense, drones and counter-drone systems, ammunition and missiles. The money would be borrowed and repaid by EU countries, not transferred to Ukraine as an aid package, and can also be spent with Ukrainian manufacturers.

author: noel_reports
text: ❗️ French President Emmanuel Macron condemned the Russian jet-powered drone strike on Dnipro railway station and said the localized ceasefire around Oleshky is not enough. He called for broader de-escalation and renewed efforts to bring Russia to the negotiating table.

author: noel_reports
text: Ukrainian manufacturer Fire Point says 90% of the components used in its drones are sourced domestically. The company says it chose technological independence three and a half years ago to reduce reliance on external events and keep production predictable.

author: noel_reports
text: A fire has been detected by NASA FIRMS after overnight Ukrainian drone activity at Marinovka Air base in Russia's Volgograd region. The fire was recorded near newly built hangars.

author: noel_reports
text: ❗️ ❗️ Russian sources report that a strike on Marinovka military airfield in Volgograd region destroyed two Su-34 fighter-bombers. The airfield is used by Russia’s 11th Composite Aviation Regiment. Two servicemen were reportedly killed and two others wounded.

author: noel_reports
text: German-made GEREON ground robots have been integrated with Ukraine’s Shablya remotely operated weapon station. The GEREON platform, produced by ARX Robotics, provides mobility, reconnaissance and observation, while the Ukrainian-made Shablya module adds remotely operated weapons. The modular system can also be adapted for logistics and casualty evacuation, and GEREON is described as the largest Western-made UGV fleet deployed in Ukraine.

author: noel_reports
text: ❗️ The Washington Sun reports that Trump administration officials are privately urging US companies to accept Russian diesel cargoes crossing the Atlantic. At least three vessels reportedly sailed for the US after Trump moved to lift sanctions on Russian diesel on October 16. Industry sources say buyers are resisting over legal and reputational risks, despite pressure and substantial discounts being offered by both Moscow and Washington.

author: noel_reports
text: Ukraine’s HUR presented debris from Russian jet-powered drones and compact cruise missiles used against Ukrainian cities. The display included Geran-3 and Geran-4 drones, as well as Banderol, Dan-T, Geran-5 and the new Filin missile. HUR also showed electronic components used for communications and navigation, saying most were of US, Chinese or European origin.

author: noel_reports
text: Operators of Ukraine’s 6th Special Operations Forces Regiment “Rangers” crossed beyond the notional frontline, raided a Russian position and captured two enemy reconnaissance troops during the operation.

author: noel_reports
text: Close-up footage recorded by a crew member aboard CONTSHIP JET shows a Russian surface drone approaching the vessel around 30 km from Shabla, Bulgaria. One of the three drones that struck the ship can be clearly identified in the video. Despite the footage, Bulgarian authorities have so far avoided directly naming Russia when commenting on the attack.

author: noel_reports
text: Putin warned Europe that a direct war with Russia would have “no winners.” Commenting on European preparations for a possible conflict with Russia by 2030, he said Moscow is ready but does not want war. “If they want to prepare, let them prepare. If the situation goes too far, there will be no winners at all. No one should forget that,” Putin said.

author: noel_reports
text: Germany’s state of Hesse will award President Volodymyr Zelensky its highest honor, the Wilhelm Leuschner Medal. Minister-President Boris Rhein said the award also recognizes the Ukrainian people for defending their sovereignty, democracy and European values against Russia’s war. Rhein praised Zelensky’s “unprecedented commitment” and said the award is a strong expression of Hesse’s continued support for Ukraine. The ceremony is set for December 1.

author: noel_reports
text: ❗️ ❗️ Russian sources report that a strike on Marinovka military airfield in Volgograd region destroyed two Su-34 fighter-bombers. The airfield is used by Russia’s 11th Composite Aviation Regiment. Two servicemen were reportedly killed and two others wounded.

text: Russian losses per 29/10/26 reported by the Ukrainian General Staff +1560 men +1 tank +5 ACVs +25 artillery +4 MLRS +1 aircraft +1614 UAVs +4 GRCs

author: noel_reports
text: Ukraine says air defenses shot down or suppressed 97 of 112 Russian drones launched overnight, including 30 of 40 jet-powered Shaheds. Seven strike drones were still airborne as of 08:00. Impacts were recorded at seven locations, with debris falling at five more.

author: noel_reports
text: ❗️ Ukrainian drones struck the Bashkir Soda Company in Sterlitamak, Bashkortostan. The facility is one of Russia’s largest chemical complexes and the country’s only producer of terephthaloyl chloride, a precursor used to make high-strength aramid fibers for body armor, helmets and ballistic protection. The plant also supplies chemicals to other Russian defense-industrial enterprises.

author: noel_reports
text: A Ukrainian delegation, including Ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets, is en route to Russian-occupied Oleshky for the planned humanitarian mission. Ukrainian sources say the group has already reached Belarus and will continue by Russian EMERCOM aircraft to Anapa, followed by onward travel to Simferopol. Representatives of Russia and the United States are also reportedly heading toward the area.

author: noel_reports
text: Former US President Barack Obama criticized the White House’s approach to Ukraine, saying: “While we are alienating key allies like Canada, the White House bends the knee to Vladimir Putin and is selling out Ukrainians fighting for their freedom and democracy.” He urged Americans to vote.

author: noel_reports
text: A fire has been detected by NASA FIRMS after overnight Ukrainian drone activity at Marinovka Air base in Russia's Volgograd region. The fire was recorded near newly built hangars.

author: noel_reports
text: ❗️ The Lugacom data center in occupied Luhansk was targeted again overnight. Additional strikes were reported in Russian-occupied Berdyansk, Mariupol and Melitopol.

author: noel_reports
text: Strikes hit multiple sites in Russian-occupied Luhansk, including the main post office, a vehicle parking area and energy infrastructure. Around 150,000 customers were reportedly left without electricity following the attack.

author: noel_reports
text: Russia claims its air defenses destroyed 1,214 drones overnight across 19 regions, including Bryansk, Belgorod, Kursk, Moscow, Rostov, Samara and Bashkortostan.

author: noel_reports
text: A Russian jet-powered drone struck the platform at Dnipro railway station as train No. 866 Dnipro-Zaporizhzhia was there, Ukrzaliznytsia says. Local media report fatalities, with people still on the platform despite the air-raid warning. There are dead and wounded.

author: noel_reports
text: ❗️ Poland will transfer two MiG-29 fighters to Ukraine as part of a new military aid package worth about €50 million, Rzeczpospolita reports. The package is also set to include artillery ammunition, 20x102mm rounds for F-16 cannons, Piorun missiles and other air-defense support.

author: noel_reports
text: A Russian jet-powered drone struck the platform at Dnipro railway station as train No. 866 Dnipro-Zaporizhzhia was there, Ukrzaliznytsia says. Local media report fatalities, with people still on the platform despite the air-raid warning. There are dead and…

author: noel_reports
text: Ukraine’s General Staff says its forces struck three Russian drone infrastructure sites near Navlya in Bryansk region, including a Geran drone storage depot, a drone launch site and fuel storage. Two radar stations near Starodub and Medvedove and two UAV command posts near Savlukove and Vitovka were also hit. A Russian command-observation post near Novohrodivka in occupied Donetsk region was struck as well.

author: noel_reports
text: Ukraine’s Defense Ministry says automated turrets destroyed dozens of Russian drones over Kyiv in the past month. Developed under Brave1 since 2024, the systems have downed more than 60 targets under the Private Air Defense project, including Banderol and Geran-5 drones.

author: noel_reports
text: Ukraine’s General Staff says Russian personnel losses in October have reached 49,040 as of October 29, the highest monthly figure recorded since the start of Russia’s full-scale invasion.

author: noel_reports
text: Footage shows a single MIM-23 Hawk air-defense missile intercepting two Russian Kalibr cruise missiles in one engagement. Ukraine’s exact inventory of Hawk launchers and interceptors is not publicly itemized. Open-source reporting indicates deliveries from several partners, including Spain and the US, are sufficient to equip roughly four batteries, with additional support focused on refurbished missiles, sustainment and parts.

author: noel_reports
text: The Netherlands will provide Ukraine with another €500 million military support package focused on air defense and drones, PM Rob Jetten announced after meeting Zelensky in The Hague. Jetten called Dutch support “rock solid” and urged Europe to continue backing Ukraine. The Netherlands will also provide €1.2 billion in non-military support over the next three years, including energy, humanitarian aid, reconstruction and demining.

author: noel_reports
text: Russian facilities are preparing for further strikes by building multi-layered mesh structures around fuel storage tanks, designed to intercept incoming strike systems before they can make contact with the tanks.

author: noel_reports
text: US Senator Richard Blumenthal has demanded that Greek shipowner EASTMED recall the Malta-flagged Agioi Fanendes, which he says left a Russian port on October 22 carrying nearly 40,000 tons of diesel and is due in New York on November 7. Blumenthal argues that a Treasury license cannot override the 2022 law banning Russian energy imports and asked the company to identify the seller, buyer, charterer, insurer and terminal operator involved.

author: noel_reports
text: Ukraine’s General Staff estimates that in more than 1,700 days of full-scale war, Russia has lost over 1.58 million personnel and more than $204 billion worth of equipment, including 12,448 tanks, 25,609 armored vehicles and 51,674 artillery systems. It says war spending rose from $86 billion in 2022 to $190 billion in 2025, with another $185 billion spent in 2026.

author: noel_reports
text: Russia has temporarily allowed grain vessels to leave the Azov Sea for the first time since July, Bloomberg reports, citing people familiar with the matter. Port authorities granted temporary clearance for departures from Temryuk and Kavkaz. At least one vessel has already passed through the Kerch Strait into the Black Sea, while ships ready to sail and with crews available can apply for clearance.

author: noel_reports
text: Russian monitoring channels are reporting a large-scale Ukrainian drone attack across multiple regions. Hundreds of UAVs were tracked through Belgorod, Kursk, Bryansk and Voronezh, with further movements reported toward Lipetsk, Kaluga, Oryol, Tula and Moscow regions. Russia claims 90 drones were already downed.

author: noel_reports
text: Zelensky met King Willem-Alexander of the Netherlands, discussing life in Ukraine under continued Russian attacks and diplomatic efforts toward peace. Zelensky called the Netherlands one of Ukraine’s closest and most reliable partners and thanked it for its continued support.

author: noel_reports
text: Zelensky and Dutch PM Rob Jetten met executives from Ukrainian and Dutch companies working in defense, energy and software. The two sides identified defense production, joint technology and energy projects, industrial development, satellite technology and air defense as key priorities. Their teams were specifically tasked with developing an air-defense project called Bliksem, with work already underway.

author: noel_reports
text: ❗️ Approximately 300 Ukrainian drones are currently in the sky over Russian and occupied regions. Launches are still ongoing.

author: noel_reports
text: All 18 crew members of the Liberian-flagged container ship CONTSHIP JET were rescued after the vessel was struck by three drones in the Black Sea near Bulgaria, according to Bulgarian authorities. The rescue operation involved emergency services, the Maritime Administration, Navy, Air Force and Border Police. No fatalities were reported.

author: noel_reports
text: Kherson has come alive during the ceasefire announced around Oleshky. Residents say the streets are suddenly full of people again, with one phrase repeated across the city: “There are so many people outside, it feels like the war has ended.”

author: noel_reports
text: A Ukrainian drone attacked a Russian military convoy near Tarkhankut in occupied Crimea. The strike narrowly missed the target by roughly a meter.

author: noel_reports
text: Satellite imagery shows damage to the D-3 and D-5 units at the Omsk Kauchuk plant following FP-1 drone strikes. Technical equipment at both installations appears to have been damaged, adding to the impact previously reported at the site.

author: noel_reports
text: 🥱 South Korean Foreign Minister Cho Hyun said Seoul could consider severing diplomatic relations with Ukraine if the current dispute continues to escalate. South Korea recalled its ambassador to Kyiv on October 8 and later withdrew eight embassy staff. The dispute centers on what Seoul says was Ukraine’s breach of a confidential agreement over the repatriation of North Korean POWs.

author: noel_reports
text: Pilots of Ukraine’s 225th Assault Regiment struck multiple Russian warehouses and logistics vehicles, targeting supply infrastructure and transport used by Russian forces.

author: noel_reports
text: Good night, sleep well and see you all tomorrow.

text: ❗️ Satellite imagery shows four Storm Shadow hits on the Energia plant in Yelets, Lipetsk region, after the Oct. 25 strike. Production buildings were heavily damaged and burned out. Energia makes power sources for Iskander, Kinzhal, Zircon, Pantsir and UMPB D-30SN systems.

author: noel_reports
text: ❗️ Occupied Crimea's energy operator says the peninsula is receiving insufficient electricity from Russia, forcing consumption restrictions across the occupied territory. The Taman substation, attacked on October 24, has not yet been fully restored, leaving the power bridge unable to supply the required capacity. Bakhchysarai district is scheduled for a five-hour outage during repair work.

author: noel_reports
text: ❗️ Ukrainian long-range drones struck the Novomoskovsk Azot chemical plant in Russia’s Tula region, with local residents reporting a fire. The plant, part of EuroChem, produces ammonia, ammonium nitrate, urea, methanol and nitric acid. Public procurement and…

author: noel_reports
text: Satellite imagery analyzed by ABSreliable shows the results of the October 24 strike in Omsk. At Omsk Kauchuk, a gas fractionation unit caught fire and the MTBE finishing unit was damaged. At Poliom, more than 40 tons of stored polypropylene burned and inter-unit pipelines suffered significant damage. The Ozon warehouse complex lost one block completely and another partially to fire.

author: noel_reports
text: Ukraine’s General Staff says Defense Forces struck several Russian military targets over the past day. A Tor-M2 air-defense system and a radar were hit in Kursk region, an electronic warfare station was struck in Bryansk region, and a Russian logistics depot was hit near Valerianivka in Donetsk region.

author: noel_reports
text: Zelensky has arrived in the Netherlands, where he is first set to meet Prime Minister Rob Jetten.

author: noel_reports
text: Russian marketplace Ozon says UAV strikes caused 30.1 billion rubles, roughly $374 million, in estimated losses in Q3 2026 after fires hit 11 logistics facilities since August. The losses include damaged goods, fixed assets and other expenses. Some risks were insured, but compensation remains under negotiation, and Ozon warns any insurance payouts may not match the scale of the losses.

author: noel_reports
text: New footage shows a Ukrainian F-16AM using an AIM-9L air-to-air missile to shoot down a Russian Geran drone over a populated area.

author: noel_reports
text: Ukraine has received another $404.5 million from Japan and the World Bank under the THRIVE project to support development of the country’s healthcare system, according to Koretskyi. The funds have already been transferred to Ukraine’s state budget and are intended to strengthen and develop the healthcare system.

author: noel_reports
text: Satellite imagery released by ABSreliable shows the aftermath of the October 10 strike on the Yug Rusi oil terminal near Bataysk in Russia’s Rostov region. Eight storage tanks were destroyed, while three more were scorched and are unlikely to return to service soon.

author: noel_reports
text: ❗️ Zelensky says trilateral talks between Ukraine, Russia and the United States could take place as early as November 10.

author: noel_reports
text: New satellite imagery obtained by RFE/RL shows Russia has expanded Gvardiiske airfield in occupied Crimea into a drone-launch hub. Ukrainian military sources say the base was first identified as a launch site in March 2025 and now sends out strike drones almost daily. Imagery from October 11 shows no visible aircraft but extensive new infrastructure and dozens of unidentified objects in the airfield’s southwest.

author: noel_reports
text: ❗️ Zelensky says the UK will provide Ukraine with an additional £10 billion in support following his call with Prime Minister Andy Burnham. £7 billion is intended for economic support over three years, while £3 billion will support exports, mainly weapons deliveries.

author: noel_reports
text: Ukraine’s HUR says its Ghosts unit carried out a series of strikes against Russian communications and electronic infrastructure. The reported targets included antenna complexes, UAV MESH repeaters, electronic warfare systems, Starlink jamming stations and electrical substations. HUR says the strikes were aimed at degrading the systems Russian forces rely on for communications, coordination and drone operations.

author: noel_reports
text: UPDATE on Oleshky: Ukraine’s Ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets says the first 30 hours of the ceasefire around Russian-occupied Oleshky passed without a single incident. He said constant communication with Russian Ombudsman Yana Lantratova helped maintain the agreement…

author: noel_reports
text: ❗️ Multiple Ukrainian sources report that Vadym Sukharevsky may replace Dmytro Delyatytskyi as commander of Ukraine’s Marine Corps. Sukharevsky was the first commander of the Unmanned Systems Forces and previously commanded the 59th Motorized Brigade. His possible appointment would bring a commander with frontline and drone-warfare experience into the role.

author: noel_reports
text: ❗️ Ukrainian long-range drones struck the Novomoskovsk Azot chemical plant in Russia’s Tula region, with local residents reporting a fire. The plant, part of EuroChem, produces ammonia, ammonium nitrate, urea, methanol and nitric acid. Public procurement and rail data cited in the reporting link it to supplies of raw materials for the Sverdlov Plant in Dzerzhinsk, a major Russian producer of military explosives.

author: noel_reports
text: ❗️ Zelensky says there is currently no progress on territorial compromises. US proposals included a buffer or demilitarized zone on both sides of the Donbas front, a possible territorial exchange around the Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant, and demilitarization of part of the Kinburn Spit while retaining Ukrainian control. He also said elections cannot be held during the war and would require at least six months of preparation for a safe process.

author: noel_reports
text: Trump says he expects to meet with Putin and Zelensky soon and believes significant progress is being made toward ending the Russia-Ukraine war. He said a meeting will be arranged “very soon” and clarified that it would involve both the Russian and Ukrainian presidents.

author: noel_reports
text: ❗️ US and Russian teams have discussed potential deals covering Russian diesel, Lukoil’s overseas assets, Nord Stream gas flows, Sakhalin-1, titanium, potash and Russian airspace access, according to Alex Raufoglu, RFE/RL’s Senior Washington Correspondent. No deals are final.

author: noel_reports
text: A 90-minute call between Putin, Finnish President Alexander Stubb and Norwegian PM Jonas Gahr Støre has sparked tensions among NATO allies, Bild reports. Denmark said the outreach was not coordinated, while Norway insists allies were informed in advance. Stubb and Støre said they acted for their own countries, not Europe as a whole, and both spoke with Zelensky before and after the call.

author: noel_reports
text: ❗️ The European Commission and European Council are preparing a joint senior-level delegation for the next Ukraine-Russia talks in November, Euronews reports. Bjoern Seibert, Ursula von der Leyen’s chief of cabinet, is expected to lead it. Brussels is openly pushing for a multilateral format bringing Europeans, Ukrainians, Americans and Russians to the same table.

author: noel_reports
text: Azov’s 1st National Guard Corps says it has struck more than 100 Russian trains carrying out logistics for Russian forces, disabling locomotives, fuel tankers and other equipment. The corps says the attacks targeted key railway stations and supply routes moving fuel toward the front, aiming to disrupt Russian frontline logistics and offensive potential.

author: noel_reports
text: Ukraine’s HUR says GROUP 10 special forces completed a seven-week operation in Sumy region, clearing more than 600 hectares of forest. The unit says it killed 108 Russian troops, captured 29 and struck over 1,100 enemy targets. HUR says the operation disrupted Russian offensive plans and prevented attempts to cut Ukrainian Defense Forces logistics routes.

author: noel_reports
text: UPDATE on Oleshky: Ukraine’s Ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets says the first 30 hours of the ceasefire around Russian-occupied Oleshky passed without a single incident. He said constant communication with Russian Ombudsman Yana Lantratova helped maintain the agreement and thanked Melania Trump for supporting the humanitarian mission. The goal is to deliver aid and create conditions for civilians who need to leave safely.

author: noel_reports
text: Zelensky says Ukraine and Trump agree on the need to end Russia’s war, but differ on the tools needed to achieve it. In an interview with The Sun, he argued that Ukrainians understand Putin and Russian society better than the United States because of their shared Soviet past and long history as neighbors. Zelensky said speaking openly and telling partners the truth is part of Ukraine’s defense strategy. He also argued that Ukraine’s decentralized digital infrastructure has helped it withstand repeated Russian attacks on data centers, while Russian systems are more centralized and therefore more vulnerable to Ukrainian retaliation.

author: noel_reports
text: Ukraine’s 26th Artillery Brigade showed the process of replacing the barrel on a Polish Krab self-propelled howitzer. Manufacturers rate the barrel for around 1,500 rounds, while Ukrainian reports say Krab barrels often reach 3,000-4,500+ rounds in combat. Some artillery systems have reportedly reached 6,000-7,000 rounds on one barrel, though accuracy and range fall sharply as wear increases.

author: noel_reports
text: ❗️ Italian PM Giorgia Meloni has reportedly frozen Italy’s 13th military aid package for Ukraine while awaiting the US midterm elections. The package is fully prepared, but no transfer date has been approved. The shipment has already been postponed several times, while Italy’s previous weapons delivery reached Ukraine 10 months ago. The government says support for Ukraine will continue, but has given neither a delivery date nor clear conditions for unblocking the package.

author: noel_reports
text: A new KIIS poll finds 63% of Ukrainians are prepared to endure the war for as long as necessary. Another 5% say one more year, 21% say several months to six months, and 11% are undecided. KIIS says there was no significant change from its October 8-16 survey, despite recent international pressure, Russian attacks and the broader campaign against Ukraine.

author: noel_reports
text: Zelensky is visiting the Netherlands today on a trip announced at the last minute. He will meet PM Rob Jetten, Deputy PM Dilan Yeşilgöz and Foreign Minister Tom Berendsen, followed by a press conference with Jetten. Later, Zelensky is due to be received by King Willem-Alexander. The Netherlands also announced €40 million in energy support for Ukraine.

author: noel_reports
text: India says the US has not pressured it to reduce Russian oil imports, according to Oil Minister Hardeep Singh Puri. He said refiners are buying more Middle Eastern crude as Gulf supplies become more competitive, while Russian purchases have declined amid stronger competition from China. Russia still remained India’s largest crude supplier.

author: noel_reports
text: Satellite imagery confirms a Ukrainian strike near the new polybutadiene production unit at Voronezhsintezkauchuk in Voronezh on October 26. CyberBoroshno had initially assessed that the facility itself was hit, but updated imagery shows a crater near the installation with no visually apparent damage to the production equipment. The Sibur-owned plant produces more than 385,000 tons of synthetic rubber and thermoplastic elastomers annually.

author: noel_reports
text: More than 100 Ukrainian drones are now moving through Russia’s Bryansk, Kaluga and Oryol regions toward Tula and Moscow regions.

author: noel_reports
text: Ukraine’s Ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets says everyone wishing to leave Russian-occupied Oleshky will be able to reach Ukrainian-controlled territory. He says the ceasefire is holding, with no violations or Russian advances recorded so far.

author: noel_reports

author: noel_reports
text: Ukraine’s Air Force says Russia is increasingly sending strike drones in small groups to complicate air-defense operations. Spokesperson Yurii Ihnat says even intercepting two Shaheds can require scrambling F-16s and covering significant distances, making each engagement demanding.

author: noel_reports
text: This smells on all sides. The Trump administration is considering lifting sanctions on the Russian Direct Investment Fund, the New York Times reports. A US official said the review is part of efforts to improve relations with Moscow and help end the war, while praising fund chief Kirill Dmitriev as a useful intermediary. The fund was sanctioned in 2022, when the Biden administration called it Putin’s “slush fund” and a symbol of Russia’s broader kleptocracy.

author: noel_reports
text: Ukraine says its interception rate against Russian Geran-4 jet-powered attack drones is steadily improving, averaging nearly 60% over the past three months and reaching up to 80% during some attacks. F-16s, Mirages and MiG-29s play a major role. Kyiv is also expanding cheaper short-range defenses, including Gepard, Skynex, Skyranger, Terrahawk Paladin, interceptor drones and mobile fire groups.

author: noel_reports
text: ❗️ Putin reportedly spent most of his call with Finnish President Alexander Stubb and Norwegian PM Jonas Gahr Støre discussing Slavic history, while a ceasefire barely came up. The call had been planned for 20 minutes but dragged on for 90. The episode underscores the difficulty European leaders face in trying to back Ukraine while engaging Putin directly ahead of peace talks.

author: noel_reports
text: Flávio Bolsonaro has left Brazil for the United States following his election defeat, Reuters reports. On Monday, he had said he never thought about leaving the country and would surrender his passports and fight what he called a clear attempt to intimidate him.

author: noel_reports
text: Missile alerts sounded across several Russian regions amid reported Ukrainian strike activity. Air defenses were active over Lipetsk against jet-powered targets. Preliminary reports indicate impacts and a fire in the direction of the local airfield, though the extent of any damage remains unclear.

author: noel_reports
text: Ukrainian FP-1 drones have recently hit three Russian rubber plants: Voronezhsintezkauchuk, Omsk Kauchuk and Tolyattikauchuk. The sector produces polymers used in solid rocket fuel, including polybutadiene-acrylonitrile, a binder and fuel component used in Iskander-M missile motors. Of roughly 10 major rubber plants in Russia, six had suffered 11 successful attacks as of October 25.

text: Denmark’s Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen criticized the Finland-Norway call with Vladimir Putin, saying the initiative had not been coordinated with other EU partners. She said Europe must preserve unity and avoid individual diplomatic initiatives.

author: noel_reports
text: ❗️ Putin told Finnish President Alexander Stubb and Norwegian PM Jonas Gahr Støre that Russia would not compromise on its goal of capturing the entire Donbas, Reuters reports, citing a source close to the Kremlin. The Nordic leaders responded that a “just” peace is needed.

author: noel_reports
text: A Russian attack on Dnipro damaged the stadium of one of the city’s lyceums, regional authorities said. Windows at the educational facility were also shattered.

author: noel_reports
text: Ukraine says it has completed its part of the pan-European FREYJA anti-ballistic project and is waiting for partner work to finish before testing. Fire Point is developing the FP-7.X interceptor and launcher; Hensoldt and Weibel are linked to radar options, Kongsberg to system integration and Diehl Defence as a possible seeker supplier. A working prototype is planned for H1 2027, with a first ballistic interception test targeted for mid-2027.

author: noel_reports
text: ❗️ Civilians leaving Russian-occupied Oleshky who want to return to Ukrainian-controlled territory will reportedly first be transported to occupied Crimea or Russia, the Financial Times reports, citing sources. Zelensky had previously warned that Russia could try to redirect evacuation routes toward its territory and then portray the movement as evidence that civilians wanted to go to Russia.

author: noel_reports
text: Similar to what happened in Hungary, Serbia’s RTV-1 publicly apologized to viewers for years of one-sided and uncritical reporting. Presenter Goran Er(r)or said the public service had failed to ask the right questions and had not fulfilled its role.

author: noel_reports
text: Kremlin aide Yury Ushakov says Finland and Norway told Putin that Zelensky wants direct talks. Putin reportedly replied that Zelensky is “illegitimate” but could come to Moscow. Ushakov said a meeting between the two leaders would make most sense only after negotiations are completed and documents are prepared. Separately, Lavrov said the war will continue and is tending to escalate.

text: Clarification : Fire Point says the FP-5 Flamingo cruise missile remains in production and that recent claims of its cancellation came from a quote taken out of context. She said the company plans to keep developing the existing model while directing most of its effort toward two ballistic missile projects.

author: noel_reports
text: Zelensky says Ukraine’s 2nd National Guard Corps “Khartiia” has killed more than 100 Russian troops and captured over 30 in Operation Veles on the Kupiansk axis. He said Ukrainian forces have advanced more than 15 km underground. Russia had previously used underground gas infrastructure to move through Ukrainian positions; Ukrainian troops adapted and modernized the tactic for the operation.

text: ❗️ Melania Trump says the humanitarian ceasefire around Russian-occupied Oleshky has been expanded beyond the city within Kherson region to provide safe passage for aid convoys. The ceasefire took effect at 03:00 Kyiv time on October 27, two days earlier than originally scheduled.

text: A large fire broke out at the Rassvet shopping complex, formerly the Traktorozavodsky market, in Volgograd on October 27. The blaze reportedly covered around 700 square meters. The cause of the fire has not been established, and no further details were provided.

text: Russia earned $2.76 billion from seaborne crude exports last week, Bloomberg reports, marking the highest weekly total since the start of the full-scale invasion. Export value jumped by about $430 million as weekly oil shipments increased sharply.

text: ❗️ Ukrainian sources say Kyiv has received no update from Pete Hegseth or the Pentagon on approvals for Patriot and NASAMS missiles, with no movement reported. Zelensky said Ukraine has been waiting nearly a month for Hegseth’s sign-off and instructed his team to raise the issue again.

author: noel_reports
text: A hole was blasted through Kyiv’s Pivdennyi Bridge during Russia’s attack, and repairs will take time. Meanwhile, Ukraine is still waiting for delayed approvals for Patriot and NASAMS interceptor missiles from Washington.

text: Ukraine’s SIGNUM unit says its drone operators struck a moving Russian vehicle column, destroying three Ural trucks before pursuing and hitting two fuel tankers. The drones were supplied by the Sternenko Community Foundation.

text: ❗️ South Korea has withdrawn eight diplomatic personnel from Ukraine amid a dispute over Kyiv’s disclosure of the transfer of two North Korean POWs. Foreign Minister Cho Hyun said Seoul had sought an explanation, an apology and assurances against a recurrence. Essential embassy staff remain in Ukraine, and Cho stressed that South Korea’s humanitarian and reconstruction support for Ukraine is unchanged.

text: Iran says it is monitoring its borders following reports that Ukraine is deploying thousands of drones in countries neighboring Iran, including Iraqi Kurdistan. The claim was reported by Tasnim on October 20, citing sources. Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei said Iran’s armed forces have responded decisively wherever they perceived a threat and would continue to do so.

author: noel_reports
text: During the humanitarian ceasefire around Oleshky, Ukrainian forces also evacuated 167 civilians from Ukrainian-controlled communities along the right bank of Kherson region. The group included 22 children and 21 people with limited mobility. The evacuation routes passed damaged and mined roads, burned military equipment and civilian vehicles, making the operation particularly difficult. The evacuees were moved to safer locations within Kherson region.

text: Russia launched 326 drones at Ukraine between 06:30 and 19:00 on November 1, including 55 jet-powered drones, plus six S8000 Banderol/Dan-T systems. Ukraine says air defenses shot down or suppressed 274 drones, including 46 jet-powered ones, and all six S8000s. More than 20 drones remain airborne.
